segments.text: When traffic surges, responders need decisions. What is happening? What should we do? And did it work?
Aegis Flow brings detection, classification, response, and verification into one operations console.
All traffic is synthetic. The baseline shows healthy source diversity and low latency.
Now we launch an HTTP flood. A small group of sources repeatedly targets the search endpoint.
The detector combines rate deviation, source and path entropy, error ratio, and connection duration to classify the attack.
We stop the first attack, arm automatic mitigation, and launch a second round. No manual rate limit is applied.
After three hot ticks, the engine applies a path rate limit. Attacking sources are capped at thirty requests per second.
Ingress stays high while origin load falls. The yellow band shows edge mitigation. Every action is logged.
Next, a flash crowd. Hundreds of diverse users are legitimate. High traffic alone does not justify blocking.
Automatic response remains armed. The engine recommends caching and leaves mitigations at zero. An operations tool earns trust by knowing when to hold back.
The AWS integration is a prototype. The repository includes a Cloud Front and WAF reference stack, plus an optional adapter for supported manual rule additions.
Offline tests check payloads, rule preservation, and locking. No live AWS deployment is claimed.
Aegis Flow makes response decisions visible. Try the browser simulation, replay an incident, and explore the code.
